b: An earlier draft of Field Manual IV quoted John D. Rockefeller as saying that the ability to keep your head when all others are losing theirs was a competitive edge. That phrasing is Rudyard Kipling's, from “If—” (1895). I could find no reliable attribution of it to Rockefeller. The point about his temperament stands; the quotation is gone.

I had repeated the standard story that John Snow removed the pump handle and stopped the 1854 outbreak. Whitehead's own figures show fatal attacks had already fallen from 142 on 1 September to 14 by the 8th, the day the handle came off, and Snow never claimed otherwise. The entry now says what the evidence says.

I had written that Harrison was finally paid the longitude prize in 1773. He received £8,750 from Parliament that year and £23,065 in total across all sources — but the statutory £20,000 was never awarded, to him or to anyone.
An early draft said roughly 6,000 miles of British railway were authorised at the peak. The 1846 figure is about 9,500 miles across 263 Acts.

Silicon & Light said an international consortium began work on extreme ultraviolet lithography in 1997. The 1997 consortium, EUV LLC, was American: Intel, AMD and Motorola with three US national laboratories. ASML was admitted in 1999, and that is when the programme became international.

The Great Divergence printed '3' as a figure — the explanations still standing. It was my own count, not a sourced number, and the entry itself discusses more than three. It is replaced by Robert Allen's estimate of the return on a spinning jenny: 38% in England against 2.5% in France.

The Unix Bargain dated the rewrite of Unix in C to 1972 and called C a language invented so the system could move. Ritchie's own account puts the kernel rewrite in the summer of 1973 and says portability carried little weight at the time; it became the point with the 1977 port to the Interdata 8/32. The entry also said Thompson wrote the first version in three weeks. By his own account it took the month his wife and son were away.
